days.note: From the Depot Creek Road trailhead (BC side, ~2,350 ft), hike past Monument 65 and up through old-growth forest and brush to Depot Creek Falls, then continue to Lake Ouzel (~5,700 ft). This is notoriously slow, bushwhacky terrain despite the modest mileage — expect roughly 6-9 hours for this leg.
days.title: Approach to Lake Ouzel

schedule.label: Leave trailhead
schedule.detail: Depot Creek Road parking, ~2,350 ft.

schedule.label: Monument 65
schedule.detail: Border marker; +500 ft.

schedule.label: Depot Creek Falls
schedule.detail: ~1,600 ft cumulative gain.

schedule.label: Arrive Lake Ouzel camp
schedule.detail: ~5,700 ft, ~3,550 ft cumulative gain.

days.objective: Reach the Lake Ouzel bivy/camp

days.note: Short but steep carry above Lake Ouzel over ledgey rock onto the toe of the Redoubt Glacier, roping up for the flat, low-crevasse-hazard glacier crossing to a rock-outcrop camp on the saddle. Many parties use this as a half-day and rest/prep gear in the afternoon.
days.title: Move to Redoubt Glacier saddle high camp
days.objective: Establish high camp at ~7,150-7,400 ft

days.note: A long roped traverse of the Redoubt Glacier (visibility can drop to ~50 yards in cloud) leads to the base of the NE ridge headwall, where two pitches of low 5th class rock gain the ridge crest before class 3-4 scrambling to the 8,407 ft summit. "Easy" is relative — this is a full, long day with real exposure and route-finding.
days.title: Summit push: Northwest Spire (Easy Mox)

schedule.label: Leave high camp
schedule.detail: Roped travel across the Redoubt Glacier.

schedule.label: Reach ridge crest
schedule.detail: Via the headwall's low 5th class rock, ~900 ft gained.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: 8.9 hr from camp; final scrambling to the 8,407 ft top.

schedule.label: Begin descent
schedule.detail: Reverse the ridge and headwall, downclimbing/rappelling as needed.

schedule.label: Back at high camp
schedule.detail: ~5.3 hr descent.

days.objective: Climb the Northeast Ridge to the NW (Easy Mox) summit and return to high camp

days.note: Break camp and reverse the full approach in one long push — down off the glacier, past Lake Ouzel, Depot Creek Falls and Monument 65 back to the road. Some parties split this into two days if the crew is tired or the crossings are running high.
days.title: Hike out
days.objective: Return to the Depot Creek trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A remote 4-day trip (strong parties compress to 3): roughly 21-24 miles round trip with ~6,000-7,000 ft of cumulative gain to the 8,407 ft summit, with two long, slow approach/exit days bracketing a hard Class 4-5 glacier-and-headwall summit day from a Redoubt Glacier saddle camp.

itinerary.cal: A remote Chilliwack peak climbed from a high camp at the head of Depot Creek. The gully to the Ridge of the Gendarmes holds snow early, and the slope to the Col of the Wild turns to loose scree later in summer.

days.note: Walk and scramble up the Depot Creek valley from about 2,300 ft to Lake Ouzel at about 5,700 ft and camp there.
days.title: Depot Creek trailhead to Lake Ouzel
days.objective: Reach a camp at Lake Ouzel (5,700 ft)

days.note: Climb from Lake Ouzel to the divide at the head of the Redoubt Glacier and Depot Creek. The move is short, which leaves time for Redoubt or a rest.
days.title: Move camp to the head of the Redoubt Glacier
days.objective: Set up a high camp near 7,200 ft

days.note: Traverse easily to the Col of the Wild, angle south on ledges onto the Ridge of the Gendarmes, pass a short vertical step and follow third-class ground to the biggest notch. Drop east to the snow gully, take the right-hand of two gullies against the spire's western walls (missing it is the usual error), and scramble to the notch under the west face. Three short pitches on very loose rock, never harder than 5.5, reach the top. Make three single-rope rappels back to the notch, downclimb the gully, and return to camp. Test every hold.

schedule.detail: About four hours from the col.

schedule.label: Back at camp
schedule.detail: Three rappels, then downclimb the gully.

days.note: Break camp and descend past Lake Ouzel and down the Depot Creek valley to the trailhead.

days.objective: Return to the car

Parties often fold in Redoubt, Spickard or the other Chilliwack peaks along the way.

Scramble the steep, often wet slabs beside the falls with the help of the fixed handline, cross the outwash plain above, and climb into the basin to camp at Ouzel Lake.

days.note: Walk or bike the 16 closed miles of Suiattle River Road from the washout to the Downey Creek trailhead first. An easy, well-graded old-growth forest trail up the Downey Creek valley to the established Sixmile Camp, used as camp one by nearly every party heading for Spire Point or the Ptarmigan Traverse. Mellow day to bank energy for the brutal Bachelor Creek day ahead.
days.title: Approach to Sixmile Camp
days.objective: Reach Sixmile Camp on the Downey Creek Trail

days.note: The crux logistics day: cross Bachelor Creek and fight through notoriously dense, wet brush on the Bachelor Creek Trail to Bachelor Meadows, cross the Cub Lake pass, then follow Itswoot Ridge (staying on talus left/west of the crest to dodge towers) to the Spire Col saddle at ~7,760 ft. Crampons typically go on around 6,800 ft where snow covers the ridge; camp at the col with big views north to Dome Glacier and Dome Peak.
days.title: Grind to Spire Col high camp

schedule.label: Leave Sixmile Camp
schedule.detail: Early start expected given the brush and distance ahead.

schedule.label: Cross Bachelor Creek, ascend to Bachelor Meadows
schedule.detail: Reportedly the wettest, brushiest section of the whole approach.

schedule.label: Cross Cub Lake pass onto Itswoot Ridge
Rope up / crampons on
schedule.detail: Where the ridge route hits continuous snow.

schedule.label: Arrive Spire Col, make camp
schedule.detail: ~7,760 ft; only the tip of Spire Point is visible from camp.

days.objective: Reach Spire Col via Bachelor Meadows, Cub Lake pass, and Itswoot Ridge

days.note: A short, exposed technical climb from camp followed by a long hike back out. From the col, an ascending traverse onto the southeast face leads up slabs to the ridge crest, across to the west side, and along airy Class 3 ledges above 1,000+ ft of exposure to the base of the summit block, which goes at Class 4-5 to a horn that fits one person. Two 60m rappels return the party to the col, where camp is broken down before retracing Itswoot Ridge, Cub Lake, and Bachelor Meadows back to Sixmile Camp.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Tiny horn, room for one; parties often take turns and linger over an hour total at the top in shifts.

schedule.label: Two 60m rappels back to the col
schedule.detail: Some parties rap from a lower ledge instead of the true summit horn.

schedule.label: Break camp, begin hike out
schedule.detail: Reverse Itswoot Ridge / Cub Lake / Bachelor Meadows.

schedule.label: Arrive Sixmile Camp
schedule.detail: Long day; some strong parties push all the way to the trailhead instead (skipping this camp).

itinerary.totalNote: A 4-day, roughly 29-mile round-trip backpack from Downey Creek Trailhead, gaining about 6,800 ft net to the 8,264 ft summit; the Bachelor Creek/Itswoot Ridge approach day is the crux of the logistics, and the summit itself is a short but airy Class 4-5 pitch with two 60m rappels to descend. Strong parties sometimes compress the return into a single long day instead of a second night at Sixmile Camp.

itinerary.cal: Best climbed June-September once Bachelor Creek brush has leafed out and snow on Itswoot Ridge has consolidated; a North Cascades National Park backcountry permit may be required for the Spire Col camp depending on exact site.

days.note: Walk or bike the 16 closed miles of Suiattle River Road from the washout to the Downey Creek trailhead first. An easy, well-graded old-growth forest trail up the Downey Creek valley to the established Sixmile Camp, used as camp one by nearly every party heading for Spire Point or the Ptarmigan Traverse. Mellow day to bank energy for the brutal Bachelor Creek day ahead.
days.title: Approach to Sixmile Camp
days.objective: Reach Sixmile Camp on the Downey Creek Trail

days.note: The crux logistics day: cross Bachelor Creek and fight through notoriously dense, wet brush on the Bachelor Creek Trail to Bachelor Meadows, cross the Cub Lake pass, then follow Itswoot Ridge (staying on talus left/west of the crest to dodge towers) to the Spire Col saddle at ~7,760 ft. Crampons typically go on around 6,800 ft where snow covers the ridge; camp at the col with big views north to Dome Glacier and Dome Peak.
days.title: Grind to Spire Col high camp

schedule.label: Leave Sixmile Camp
schedule.detail: Early start expected given the brush and distance ahead.

schedule.label: Cross Bachelor Creek, ascend to Bachelor Meadows
schedule.detail: Reportedly the wettest, brushiest section of the whole approach.

schedule.label: Cross Cub Lake pass onto Itswoot Ridge
Rope up / crampons on
schedule.detail: Where the ridge route hits continuous snow.

schedule.label: Arrive Spire Col, make camp
schedule.detail: ~7,760 ft; only the tip of Spire Point is visible from camp.

days.objective: Reach Spire Col via Bachelor Meadows, Cub Lake pass, and Itswoot Ridge

days.note: A short, exposed technical climb from camp followed by a long hike back out. From the col, an ascending traverse onto the southeast face leads up slabs to the ridge crest, across to the west side, and along airy Class 3 ledges above 1,000+ ft of exposure to the base of the summit block, which goes at Class 4-5 to a horn that fits one person. Two 60m rappels return the party to the col, where camp is broken down before retracing Itswoot Ridge, Cub Lake, and Bachelor Meadows back to Sixmile Camp.
days.title: Summit Spire Point, hike back to Sixmile Camp

schedule.label: Leave Spire Col camp for the base of the climb
schedule.detail: ~0.25 mi along the ridge to the start of the route.

schedule.label: Reach the ridge crest, traverse west-side ledges
schedule.detail: Class 3 with major exposure over the west face.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Tiny horn, room for one; parties often take turns and linger over an hour total at the top in shifts.

schedule.label: Two 60m rappels back to the col
schedule.detail: Some parties rap from a lower ledge instead of the true summit horn.

schedule.label: Break camp, begin hike out
schedule.detail: Reverse Itswoot Ridge / Cub Lake / Bachelor Meadows.

schedule.label: Arrive Sixmile Camp
schedule.detail: Long day; some strong parties push all the way to the trailhead instead (skipping this camp).

days.objective: Climb Spire Point via the southwest/southeast face, then descend to Sixmile Camp

days.note: A straightforward, mostly downhill walk back down the Downey Creek Trail to the car, closing out the ~29-mile round trip.
days.title: Hike out to trailhead
days.objective: Return to Downey Creek Trailhead

itinerary.totalNote: A 4-day, roughly 29-mile round-trip backpack from Downey Creek Trailhead, gaining about 6,800 ft net to the 8,264 ft summit; the Bachelor Creek/Itswoot Ridge approach day is the crux of the logistics, and the summit itself is a short but airy Class 4-5 pitch with two 60m rappels to descend. Strong parties sometimes compress the return into a single long day instead of a second night at Sixmile Camp.

days.note: Hike the Downey Creek Trail and the brushy Bachelor Creek path to camp at Bachelor Flats (about 4,500 ft), or push on to Cub Lake (long day with significant brush and blowdown on Bachelor Creek).
days.title: Day 1

days.note: Over the pass to Cub Lake, up Itswoot Ridge and across the Dome Glacier to a high camp at the Dome-Chickamin col (about 8,500 ft).
days.title: Day 2

days.note: Cross the Chickamin Glacier to the base of the West Face, climb the route (5-6 pitches), rappel, and return to the col. Days 4-5: Hike out over Itswoot Ridge and Cub Lake and down the Bachelor Creek and Downey Creek trails. Carry a spare day for weather.
